ov: Small birds with big heads, short tails and strong bills and feet, mostly blue-grey above with a black eye stripe. Most live in woods of the Northern Hemisphere and nest in holes; the name comes from wedging nuts in cracks and hacking them open.
rg: Woods of North America, Europe and Asia, with a few in North Africa (Algeria and Morocco).
df: Mainly insects such as caterpillars and beetles, plus nuts and seeds in autumn and winter.
fx: If a nest hole is too big, the female Eurasian nuthatch plasters it with mud to shrink it.
The Eurasian nuthatch stores food all year round.
